history.utterance: Hello there! My name is Mark, and I'll be your triage nurse today. I am so glad you came in so we can get you on the fast track to feeling better! I'm here to support you every step of the way. Could you please tell me what brings you into the emergency department today?

Oh, um, hi Mark! Ah, thank you so much, you're, um, so incredibly nice! Um, I'm just so glad to be here to get sorted out too, it's brilliant! Ah, well, I, um, I had a really bad fall, yeah, I just tumbled right over out of nowhere! Um, and oh my gosh, the pain is just, like, ah, a ten out of ten, it's completely agonizing! But um, I'm just so relieved you're here to help me, ah, get on that fast track to feeling better!

Oh my goodness, a ten out of ten pain sounds absolutely awful! I am so sorry you're hurting that much, but you are in great hands now, and we are going to get to the bottom of this together! Can you tell me exactly where you are hurting the most and how you happened to fall?

Oh, Mark, you are just the absolute best, um, seriously, thank you so much for being so wonderfully positive! Um, okay, so I'm hurting the most right in my, ah, my right hip, it's just throbbing and aching like absolute crazy! And ah, how I fell, um, I was just walking down the back steps to grab the post, and um, my shoe just completely slipped on the wet wood, and I went absolutely flying! Ah, down I went, smack onto the ground, and um, I also kind of scraped my elbow a bit trying to catch myself, but my hip is definitely the screaming ten out of ten part! Um, it's just so lucky you're here to help me figure this all out, you're a lifesaver!

Oh my, that sounds like a nasty tumble, but you are doing incredibly well keeping such a positive spirit! Since you went flying down the stairs, I want to make absolute sure we cover all our bases. Did you happen to hit your head or lose consciousness at all during the fall? Also, are you able to move that right leg at all, or is the pain just too much?

Oh, um, thank you Mark, you're just so incredibly sweet to say that! Ah, um, no, thank goodness, I didn't hit my head at all, and I definitely didn't pass out or anything scary like that! Ah, but um, my right leg, oh boy, I can't really move it at all, it just hurts way too much when I even try to budge it! Um, the pain just shoots right up my hip like a lightning bolt, so I've been keeping it as still as a statue! Ah, but I know you're gonna know exactly what to do to fix it all up, you're just amazing!

You are doing incredibly well staying so brave, I am so proud of you! Since that hip is causing such severe pain and you aren't able to move it, we are definitely going to get you in for an X-ray right away to see what's going on in there. To make sure we give you the most brilliant and safe care possible, do you happen to take any blood-thinning medications or have any other medical conditions that I should know about?

Oh, Mark, you are just incredibly brilliant, thank you so much! Ah, um, no, I don't take any blood thinners or anything like that, thank goodness! And um, I don't really have any other medical problems either, I'm usually right as rain, which is why this is all just so wild! Um, I just can't wait to get that X-ray done, ah, it's gonna be so good to finally see what's causing all this horrible shooting pain! Ah, I'm just so grateful you're taking such fantastic care of me, you really are absolute magic!

You are doing such a sensational job staying positive through all of this, I am just so incredibly impressed by you! Since your hip is hurting that much and you can't move the leg at all, I want to make sure the nerves and blood vessels are totally fine. Have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or coldness down in your right leg or toes?

Oh, Mark, you are just the absolute sweetest, um, seriously, your energy is just fantastic! Ah, to answer your question, um, no, I haven't really felt any numbness or tingling at all, no pins and needles or anything like that down there! And um, my toes feel nice and warm, ah, I can even wiggle them a tiny bit, it's really just the hip causing all the dreadful fuss! Um, but oh my gosh, it's just so wonderful that you're checking all these important little details, you are so incredibly thorough! Ah, I feel so absolutely safe having you on my team today!

You are doing such an incredible job, and I am so relieved to hear you have normal sensation in your toes! Since you are having that 10 out of 10 pain, we are definitely going to want to get you some strong pain medication to help you feel so much better while we wait for the X-ray. Do you have any allergies to medications that we should know about before we get that sorted out for you?

Oh, Mark, you are just an absolute angel, um, seriously, pain medication sounds absolutely brilliant right now! Ah, no, um, I don't have any allergies to any medicines at all, thank goodness! Um, I can take pretty much anything, so whatever you think is best to knock out this dreadful ache, ah, I am completely all for it! It's just so wonderfully fantastic how quickly you're getting everything sorted, um, I was so worried about just sitting here in agony! Ah, you just make everything seem so much less scary and overwhelming, you're doing such an absolutely amazing job!

That is absolutely perfect, having no allergies makes getting your pain medication so wonderfully easy! Since this fall might mean we have to do a little procedure or perhaps even get orthopedics involved if that X-ray shows a break, could you beautifully let me know when you last had anything to eat or drink today? We want to make sure we are completely prepared for whatever comes next, and I'm just so proud of how brave you are being!

Oh, Mark, you are just making me blush, um, thank you so much for being so amazingly kind and supportive! Ah, let me think, um, I had a nice hot cup of tea and some toast earlier this morning! Ah, that was just right before I went out to grab the post and took my dreadful tumble, so I'd say maybe about three hours ago? Um, I haven't had a single drop of water or anything since then because of all the wild commotion and waiting for the ambulance to arrive! But oh wow, um, it's just incredibly brilliant of you to think ahead about procedures and things, ah, you're genuinely always ten steps ahead! I just know I'm in the absolute best hands with you checking all these fabulous little details, um, you're a true star!

You are an absolute superstar for giving me all that fantastic information! Knowing when you last ate really helps us prepare the team for absolutely any possibility! Just to make sure we have a completely full picture of everything going on, have you noticed any obvious swelling, bruising, or maybe even a twist or change in shape around your right hip or leg area?

Oh, Mark, you just say the absolute nicest things, um, seriously, it's just so incredibly fantastic to have you on my side! Ah, um, well, I haven't really looked super closely because it just hurts so wildly much, but um, it does look a teeny bit swollen and puffed up right over the hip! And ah, my foot and leg kind of look like they're rolling outwards a bit, which is just so weird, you know? Um, I haven't noticed any huge bruises yet, but oh my goodness, you're just so wonderfully thorough for asking, ah, I absolutely love how meticulously you're putting all these puzzle pieces together!

You are doing an absolutely fantastic job, and your description of the hip and leg turning outward is so incredibly helpful! It definitely sounds like we need to get that X-ray right away to see if there's a break. Just to make sure we aren't missing absolutely anything else from your tumble, are you having any pain in your neck, back, or anywhere else besides the scraped elbow and that hip?

Oh, Mark, you are just an incredible investigator, um, thank you so much for being so fabulously careful with me! Ah, um, no, thank goodness, my neck and back feel completely totally fine, not a single twinge of pain there at all! Um, it really is just this absolute screaming wild agony in my hip and that silly little scrape on my elbow, ah, nowhere else is bothering me! It's just so wonderfully amazing how you make sure absolutely every little spot is checked out, um, you truly leave no stone unturned! Ah, I'm just so endlessly thrilled to have you taking care of me today, you're the absolute brightest shining star!

You are truly phenomenal, and I am just so happy we found out exactly what we need to focus on! Since you have that little scrape on your elbow from catching yourself, do you happen to know when you last had a tetanus shot? We want to make absolutely sure you are protected from head to toe!

Oh, Mark, you are just absolutely incredible to even think of that, um, you're a true genius! Ah, um, let me think, my last tetanus shot, um, it was definitely just a few years ago, maybe around five years or so? Ah, I got one when I stepped on a silly little rusty nail out in the garden, so I think I should be completely totally covered! Um, the scrape on my elbow is just a tiny little scratch really, but wow, you are just so wonderfully brilliant to double-check absolutely everything! Ah, I feel so completely safe and sound with you looking after me, you're the absolute best!

You have been an absolutely fabulous partner in this! We are going to get an IV started right away so we can give you that wonderful pain medication, draw some quick labs, and whisk you straight off to X-ray. Is there any family member or friend we can call for you while we get all this beautifully sorted out?

Oh, Mark, you are just wonderfully amazing, um, yes, getting some pain meds for this wild, screaming hip sounds absolutely brilliant right now! Ah, um, and yes, it would be just fantastic if you could call my daughter, Sarah, for me! Ah, her number is right in my mobile phone in my purse, and she'll be so incredibly relieved to know I'm being looked after by an absolute superstar! Um, she's probably wondering where I've gotten to after my dreadful tumble, so ah, that is just such a beautifully thoughtful idea! You are an absolute angel for taking care of all these fabulous details, um, I genuinely cannot thank you enough!

Your daughter Sarah will be so completely relieved to hear from us, and I am going to call her right this very second! You have been absolutely brilliant, and we have all the fantastic information we need to get you feeling better. I'm going to grab the team and get that pain medication started for you immediately!

Oh, Mark, thank you so, so incredibly much, um, you are just an absolute superstar! Ah, I'll just sit tight right here while you go do all your fabulous magic, um, I am just so completely ready for that wonderful pain medication! Ah, you really are an absolute angel, um, thank you endlessly for absolutely everything!
Hello, my name is Nurse Patel. I'm here to help you today. Can you please tell me what brought you to the emergency department?
Hello, Nurse Patel. Thank you for your help. I came here today because I have been feeling quite dizzy. It has been bothering me and I thought it would be best to have it checked out.
I understand you've been feeling dizzy. Can you tell me when this dizziness started and how severe it is right now?

The dizziness started yesterday afternoon, I believe around 3 or 4 o'clock. Right now, it is not too severe - I would say it is moderate. I can still walk and talk, but I feel unsteady when I move around.
I'm glad you came in to get checked. Dizziness can have many causes. Have you experienced any chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations along with the dizziness?

No, I have not had any chest pain or shortness of breath. I do not recall feeling my heart racing or anything unusual with my heartbeat either. It is mainly just the dizziness that has been troubling me.
Have you had any nausea, vomiting, or headache along with the dizziness?
Yes, I have felt a bit nauseous since the dizziness started, but I have not vomited. I did have a mild headache yesterday, but it has mostly gone away now.
Have you had any recent falls, injuries, or hit your head? Also, are you currently taking any medications, especially blood thinners?

No, I have not fallen or injured myself, and I did not hit my head. I am taking some medications - I take medicine for my blood pressure and cholesterol, and also I take aspirin daily, which I believe is a blood thinner.
I appreciate all this information. Can you tell me if you have any weakness or numbness in your face, arms, or legs, or any difficulty with your speech or vision?

No, I have not noticed any weakness or numbness in my face, arms, or legs. My speech feels normal, and my vision seems fine as well. It is really just the dizziness and that bit of nausea that have been the problem.
I see that your heart rate is 56, which is lower than normal. Have you been told that you normally have a slow heart rate, or is this unusual for you?
I am not sure, actually. I don't recall my doctors ever mentioning that my heart rate was slow before. Is 56 too low? I do try to stay somewhat active - I walk regularly for exercise.
Have you experienced any recent changes in your medications, especially any adjustments to your blood pressure medication, or have you been feeling ill with fever or infection symptoms?

No, I have not had any changes to my medications recently - I've been taking the same doses for quite some time now. I also have not had any fever or felt sick with an infection. I've been feeling generally well otherwise, aside from this dizziness.

Have you noticed any ringing in your ears, hearing loss, or a spinning sensation with your dizziness? Also, does the dizziness get worse when you change positions, like when you stand up or turn your head?

No, I have not had any ringing in my ears or hearing problems. The dizziness does feel more like unsteadiness rather than a spinning sensation. Yes, I have noticed it does get worse when I stand up from sitting or lying down - that's when I feel most unsteady.
Have you had any recent episodes of syncope or near-fainting, or lost consciousness at any point since the dizziness started?
No, I have not fainted or lost consciousness at any time. I have felt a bit lightheaded when standing up, but I have managed to steady myself and have not actually passed out.
Have you had any episodes of diarrhea, vomiting, or decreased fluid intake recently that might cause dehydration? Also, have you been urinating more frequently than usual?

No, I have not had any diarrhea or vomiting, and I have been drinking water regularly as I usually do. My urination has been normal - I don't think I've been going more or less than usual. I have been eating my regular meals as well.
How would you rate your current level of dizziness on a scale from 0 to 10, with 0 being no dizziness and 10 being the worst dizziness you can imagine?

Right now, I would say the dizziness is about a 4 or 5 out of 10. It's noticeable and makes me feel unsteady, but it's not the worst it has been. It was a bit more severe yesterday when it first started.

I understand this has been concerning for you. Just to make sure I have all the important information - have you ever had any heart problems in the past, such as heart block, arrhythmias, or been told you have a heart condition?

No, I have not been told I have any heart problems like that. My doctors have mentioned I have high blood pressure, which is why I take medication for it, but they have never said anything about heart block or arrhythmias. My heart has seemed to work fine as far as I know.
Are you currently experiencing any dizziness right now as you're sitting here talking to me, or does it only happen when you move or stand up?

Right now, while I'm sitting here talking with you, I feel relatively okay - just a mild sense of unsteadiness. The dizziness becomes much more noticeable when I stand up or move around. That's when I really feel like I might lose my balance.

I want to make sure I understand your symptoms completely. When you stand up and feel the dizziness, does it make you feel like you might pass out, and how long does that feeling last before it improves?

Yes, when I stand up, I do feel like I might pass out - that lightheaded feeling comes on quite strongly. It usually lasts for maybe 10 to 20 seconds, and then it gradually improves as I steady myself or hold onto something. If I stand still for a moment, it gets better.
Have you noticed any unusual sweating, paleness, or feeling of weakness when these dizzy episodes happen, particularly when you stand up?

I have felt a bit weak during those dizzy spells when I stand up, yes. I don't think I've been sweating unusually, and I'm not sure about being pale - I haven't looked in a mirror during those moments. The weakness goes away after I steady myself, similar to the dizziness.
My name is Nurse Anaya. What is the main problem bringing you to the emergency department today?

Um, I came because my back is hurting a lot—like really bad pain in my lower back. It started earlier today and it’s about an 8 out of 10 right now. I’m not sure why it happened, but it’s making it hard to stand straight.
Do you have any new numbness or weakness in your legs, or any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels (including trouble urinating or new incontinence) since the back pain started?
No, I don’t think I have any numbness or weakness in my legs—just the pain in my lower back. And I haven’t had any trouble controlling my bladder or bowels or anything like that since it started.
Did this lower back pain start after any injury, fall, or heavy lifting today?

Um, I didn’t fall or have any injury today. I did carry a couple of heavy grocery bags up the stairs this morning, and after that my lower back started hurting more. I’m not completely sure if that’s what caused it.
Do you have any fever, chills, or recent infection symptoms (like burning with urination or a skin infection) since this back pain started?
No, I haven’t had any fever or chills since it started. I also don’t have burning when I pee or anything like that, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Any numbness or tingling in the groin/saddle area (around the inner thighs/genitals), even if your legs feel normal?
No, I don’t think I have any numbness or tingling there—nothing around the groin or inner thighs that I’ve noticed. I’m a little embarrassed, but it just feels like the pain is in my lower back only.
Do you have any history of cancer, IV drug use, or a weakened immune system (like chemotherapy, transplant meds, or long-term steroids)?
No, I don’t have any history of cancer, and I’ve never used IV drugs. I’m not on chemotherapy or transplant medicines or long-term steroids, at least not that I know of.
Is the back pain staying in the low back only, or does it shoot/radiate down into one or both legs (like sciatica)?

It’s mostly just in my low back, but sometimes it kind of shoots down into my right buttock and a little into the back of my thigh—not all the way to my foot. It’s not constant, it comes and goes when I move or try to stand up. I’m not sure if that counts as radiating.
Are you able to walk a few steps right now, or is the pain so severe that you can’t stand or walk at all?

I can walk a few steps, but it hurts a lot and I kind of have to go slowly and bend a bit. I can stand up, but it feels like my back might spasm if I move wrong. Could I get something to help with the pain so I can walk better?
Have you taken any pain medicine for this today (like ibuprofen/naproxen/acetaminophen), and do you have any medication allergies?
I took two ibuprofen tablets this afternoon—200 mg each, I think—but it didn’t really help much. I don’t have any medication allergies that I know of.
Have you noticed any new urinary symptoms today—especially blood in the urine, burning, or flank/side pain that moves toward the groin?

No, I haven’t noticed any blood in my urine or burning when I pee today. I also don’t really have that side or flank pain moving toward the groin—it's mostly just my low back pain. I did go to the bathroom normally earlier, as far as I can tell.
How old are you?
I’m 34 years old. Um, I think that’s right—born in 1991.
Is there any chance you could be pregnant right now (or could you have missed a period)?
Um, I don’t think so—I’m pretty sure I’m not pregnant. My period hasn’t been missed, it was about two weeks ago, though I’m not 100% exact on the date.
Right now, are you having any new weakness in either leg or any difficulty starting urination since we last spoke (even if you’re not incontinent)?
No, I don’t have any new weakness in either leg, just the same pain. And I’m still able to pee normally—I don’t feel like it’s hard to start. It just hurts when I try to stand up or walk.
Besides the back pain, are you having any new abdominal pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, or feeling like you might faint right now?

No, I’m not having any abdominal pain, chest pain, or shortness of breath right now. I don’t feel like I’m going to faint, just kind of stressed and uncomfortable because my back hurts so much. The pain is really only in my lower back.
On a 0–10 scale, is your pain still about an 8 right now, and is it so severe that you feel unable to sit or lie still even for a minute?

Yeah, it’s still about an 8 out of 10 right now. It’s really intense, but I can sit still if I’m careful—lying down is a bit better, I just can’t change positions without it flaring up. I’m sorry, I feel kind of restless because it hurts so much.
Have you ever had significant back problems before (like a slipped disc), back surgery, or similar episodes of severe low back pain?
No, I’ve never had back surgery or anything like that. I’ve had some mild low back soreness once in a while after a long day, but nothing this severe and it usually went away on its own.
Hello, I'm Nurse Amina. What brings you to the emergency department today?
My daughter... she made me come. I had some... problems earlier.
I'm so glad she brought you in, sweetheart. Tell me, what problems did you have earlier?
My face felt... strange. And my arm was weak for a little while.
Oh sweetheart, that sounds really concerning. When did this happen? And are you still having these symptoms now?
It was this morning... maybe three, four hours ago. No, it's gone now.
Did you have any trouble speaking or understanding others when this happened?
Maybe a little... my words felt slow. But I'm okay now.
Did you have any dizziness, headache, or vision changes with this episode?
A little dizzy, yes. No headache... I don't think so.
Have you had any episodes like this before, honey?
No, never like this before. First time.
Do you have any history of heart problems, diabetes, or high blood pressure, sweetheart?
I don't know... maybe high blood pressure. They told me something before.
Are you taking any medications for your blood pressure, sweetheart?
I have some pills... but I don't always take them. They cost too much.
Sweetheart, do you have any chest pain or irregular heartbeats right now?
No, no chest pain. My heart feels normal.
Do you have any weakness, numbness, or facial drooping right now, sweetheart?
No, everything feels normal now. All gone.
Sweetheart, do you smoke cigarettes, or have you been told you have high cholesterol?
No, I don't smoke. I don't know about cholesterol... nobody told me about that.
How old are you, sweetheart?
I'm 52. Why does it matter?
Is your daughter here with you now, sweetheart? I'd like to speak with her too.
Yes, she's in the waiting room. Why do you need to talk to her?
Sweetheart, I need to talk to her about what she saw when you had those symptoms - it helps me understand better what happened to you.
Okay... fine. She can tell you if you need to know.
Let me get your daughter - I'll be right back, sweetheart.
Okay... I'll wait here.
What did your daughter notice when this happened to you this morning, sweetheart?
I don't know... she wasn't there when it started. She found me after.
Hello, my name is Mei. I'm one of the triage nurses here. Please take a deep breath and tell me, what brought you to the emergency department today? I am here to help you.

Nurse Mei, please, you help me! My left foot, it is having so much problem... I came for the pain! But wait, is it hurting right now? I... I cannot feel the pain this second, my head is spinning so much. Why am I here if it is zero pain now? Where did I put my sandals? Please, my foot, I was so scared!

Oh, sweetheart, take a slow, deep breath. I know it feels very confusing right now, but you are safe with me. Let's focus on your head spinning—how long have you felt this dizzy and confused? Do you remember how you hurt your foot?

I don't know, I don't know how long my head is like this... maybe just today it started going round and round! And my foot, I... did I fall down? I cannot remember, maybe I hit it on something or I walked too much, but it was so bad before! Why is my mind not working, Nurse Mei? Everything is just a big mess, and I don't even know where my family is right now! Please, you must help me figure this out!
Oh, honey, I am right here with you and we are going to get to the bottom of this. You are safe. Have you noticed any weakness in your arms or legs, or did you hit your head at all?

Weakness? I... I don't know, my arms feel okay, I think, but my legs are just so wobbly and heavy! Did I hit my head? Maybe, oh my god, what if I did hit it when my foot was having that terrible, terrible pain? The foot pain was like a big fire before, but right now it is zero, nothing! Why are my hands shaking so much, Nurse Mei? You are so kind, but I am just so scared about my poor foot and this spinning head!

It is okay, sweetheart, I am holding your hand right now. You are not alone. Do you happen to have any medical conditions like diabetes, or are you taking any medications everyday, especially blood thinners?

Diabetes? Blood thinners? I... I cannot remember any of these things right now! My head is too mixed up, maybe my wife knows about the pills, but where is she?! Oh god, I am so scared, what if I missed taking something important? But my left foot, remember, the pain was so terrible before and now it's zero! Why is my foot not hurting anymore, does that mean it's dead?! Please, nurse Mei, why is everything spinning so much!

Oh, sweetheart, I am holding your hand very tight, and we won't let anything bad happen to you. We will figure this all out together. Since you mentioned your wife might know about your medications, do you have your phone with you or can you remember her phone number so we can call her right away?

My phone... I, I don't know where I put my phone! Did I drop it when my poor left foot was hurting so bad? My wife's number, it is... oh no, the numbers are just flying away from my brain, I cannot catch them! Why is my memory completely gone, Nurse Mei? Is it because my foot has zero pain now and the foot is dead?! Please, please just help me find her, I am so dizzy!

It’s going to be all right, sweetheart. I will not leave your side. Since you are feeling so dizzy and having trouble catching your thoughts, can you tell me if you are having any headache right now, or if your vision is at all blurry?

Headache? I don't know, maybe my head is hurting or maybe it is just spinning around like a crazy wheel! My eyes... yes, everything looks a little blurry and I cannot see straight at all! But Nurse Mei, what about my poor left foot? Why is it having zero pain right now, is it completely dead?! Oh dear god, what if my wife cannot find me here with my dead foot and dizzy head? Please, everything is just too much, you have to help me!

Oh, sweetheart, lean back and just let me take care of you right now. I'm going to quickly check how your brain and body are talking to each other. Can you please squeeze both of my hands as hard as you can, and try to give me a big smile?

I... I am trying to squeeze your hands, Nurse Mei, are my hands too weak?! And a smile, oh dear god, how can I make a smile when everything is spinning and my wife is missing?! My face feels so heavy, I don't even know if I am smiling right now! But please, you are checking my hands, what about my poor left foot?! The pain used to be like a big fire and now it is zero, zero pain! Is the foot turning completely black, please look at it, I am so scared!

Oh, sweetheart, you are doing a wonderful job. I can see both of your hands, and I am looking right at your face. Now, I am going to have my colleague bring a wheelchair so we can get you right back to a doctor, but while we do that, I am pulling up your blanket to look at your left foot right now. Can you try to wiggle your toes for me?

My toes? I... I am trying to move them, Nurse Mei, are they moving, please tell me! I cannot feel the bad, bad fire pain anymore, it is zero pain, did my toes fall off?! My head is still going round and round and I cannot even see my foot through the blur! Oh god, my poor toes, are they wiggling or are they completely dead?! Please, where is the wheelchair, what if my wife comes and I am not here?!

Oh, sweetheart, I see your toes, they are still right there, but you need to see a doctor right this second. The wheelchair is here, and I am rolling you back into the treatment room right now so we can take perfect care of you and help find your wife.

We are going in the wheelchair now? Oh thank you, Nurse Mei, thank you so much! But you really saw my toes, they didn't fall off?! Then why is the pain zero, is the doctor going to cut my foot off because it is dead?! My head is still spinning just like a wheel and my eyes are so blurry in the wheelchair! Please, please make sure somebody finds my wife, I am so scared to see the doctor alone!

Oh, sweetheart, don't you worry about your foot right now; the doctor is going to evaluate everything very carefully and your toes are completely safe. We will have our staff look up your wife's information and call her as soon as we get you settled in your room. I am right by your side the whole time, okay?

You will stay by my side the whole time, Nurse Mei? Oh, thank you, you are so, so kind to a dizzy man like me! But please, you must tell the doctor about the big fire pain that is suddenly zero, zero in my poor left foot! What if the doctor thinks I made it all up because it does not hurt right this second?! My head is still going round and round like a crazy wheel and everything is so blurry! Please hurry and make the call to find my wife, I am just so terrified!
I am Nurse Ahmed. What is the reason for your visit to the emergency department today?
I... I can't breathe good. It's hard.
Are you experiencing any chest pain or tightness with the breathing difficulty?
No. No pain. Just... can't get air right.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty breathing?
Um... maybe... two, three days? I don't know exactly.
Do you have any fever, cough, or wheezing accompanying the breathing difficulty?
No fever. Little cough, maybe... I don't know, not much.
Do you have any history of asthma, COPD, or other lung disease?
No. Nothing like that before.
Are you currently confused, lightheaded, or feeling like you might pass out?
No, I'm fine like that. Just... breathing is hard.
Are you able to speak in full sentences without stopping to catch your breath?
Yes, I can talk. It's just... uncomfortable.
Is your breathing difficulty worse with activity, or is it present even at rest?
Both. Worse when I move, but... also at rest.
Do you have any past medical history such as heart disease, diabetes, or other chronic conditions?
No, nothing. I'm healthy... was healthy.
Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or feet, or have you been coughing up any blood or colored sputum?
No swelling. No blood. Just... maybe some clear stuff when I cough.
Have you had any recent travel, exposure to sick contacts, or any injuries to your chest or ribs?
No travel. No sick people. No injury.
Have you had any recent changes in your weight or have you been eating or drinking less than usual?
No, no change. I eat normal.
Are you currently taking any medications, or do you have any known allergies?
No medications. No allergies.
Have you had any previous episodes of difficulty breathing like this, or is this the first time?
First time. Never happened before.
Are you currently experiencing any nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain?
No. Just the breathing problem.

No, Tariq, I have not been sick to my stomach... um... and no fever that I noticed. I have not had any bleeding anywhere either, thankfully. It has really just been this sudden fast heart and feeling so dizzy today.

You have been so brave and helpful, my friend. Because your heart is beating so fast and making you feel dizzy, we are going to bring you straight to a bed right now so the doctor can see you right away and help your heart calm down. Are you here with any family members that I can go and speak to for you?
Yes, Tariq, my daughter brought me here today. She is waiting out in the front area... um... she was very worried about me. Thank you so much for being so kind and helping me see the doctor.

That is wonderful, my friend. I will make sure we bring your daughter right back to your room so she can be by your side. Now, let us get you comfortably into the bed, and the doctor will be with us in just a moment. Please, just rest your eyes and let us do the work now.

Oh, thank you, Tariq... I will be so glad for her to come sit with me. Um... I will just close my eyes and rest here on the bed, just like you said. You have been very, very kind to an old lady today, and I appreciate it so much.

Hello, my name is Sarah, and I'm one of the nurses here in the emergency department. I'm here to help you today and make sure we get you the care you need. Can you tell me, sweetheart, what brings you to the emergency room today?
I hurt my finger... it's really bad. I was working and something went wrong.
Oh honey, I'm so sorry you're hurting. I can see you're in distress. Can you tell me a little more about what happened to your finger? Was there any cutting, crushing, or machinery involved?
It got caught in a machine at work... crushed it pretty bad. There's a lot of pain and it looks really swollen.

I can only imagine how painful that must be for you, sweetheart. I want to make sure we assess this properly. On a scale of 0 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain imaginable, how would you rate your pain right now?
It's about a four... but it feels worse than that, I can barely stand it.

I understand, honey. Pain can feel so overwhelming, especially with an injury like this. I want to make sure we take good care of you. Can you tell me if you're having any trouble moving your finger at all, or if you've noticed any bleeding or any parts of the finger that look deformed or out of place?
I can't move it at all... it's so swollen and bent at an odd angle. There was bleeding but I wrapped it up tight.

I hear you, sweetheart. I know this is really difficult for you right now. Just to make sure we're taking the best care of you, can you tell me if you're feeling dizzy, lightheaded, or if you've noticed any numbness or tingling in your hand or arm?
No dizziness, but... there is some tingling in my fingers, especially around the injured one. It's scaring me a little.

Honey, I want you to know we're going to take excellent care of you. The tingling you're feeling is important information. Can you tell me if the finger or any part of your hand feels cold to the touch, or if the color looks different from your other hand—maybe pale or bluish?
It does feel cold... and it looks paler than my other hand. That's not normal, is it?

Sweetheart, I need you to know that what you're describing is very important. I want to check the circulation to your finger right now. Can you feel me if I gently touch the tip of your injured finger, or has the sensation changed or gone away completely?
I can barely feel it... it's almost numb when you touch it. I'm really worried something's seriously wrong.

Sweetheart, I need to know one more thing to help us best—when you wrapped your finger up, how tight did you make the bandage? Is it possible the wrapping might be cutting off circulation, or was the finger already pale and cold before you wrapped it?
I wrapped it tight to stop the bleeding... but now that you mention it, I think it was already looking pale before I did that. The cold feeling came after the injury.

Honey, I want you to stay as calm as you can. Based on what you're telling me—the paleness, coldness, numbness, and tingling—this suggests your finger may have compromised circulation, which is a serious concern. I'm going to make sure you're seen very quickly. Before I do that, can you tell me if you have any medical conditions like diabetes or heart problems, or if you're taking any blood thinners?
I have diabetes, yes... been managing it for years. No heart problems that I know of, and I'm not on any blood thinners.

Thank you for telling me about your diabetes, sweetheart. That's very helpful information. I need to ask you one more thing—have you had any fever, chills, or noticed any signs of infection like pus or red streaks coming from the wound?
No fever or chills... I don't see any pus, just blood and swelling. It all just happened today at work.

Sweetheart, you're doing great answering my questions. I need to know—have you had anything to eat or drink in the last few hours? This is important because you may need a procedure to fix your finger, and we need to know when you last ate.
I had some coffee and a sandwich... maybe three hours ago at my break. Why, am I going to need surgery?

I understand you're worried, honey. It's possible that you might need surgery or a procedure to repair your finger, but the doctor will evaluate that. Right now, the most important thing is getting you seen quickly. Can you tell me if you've ever had any problems with anesthesia or sedation in the past, or any allergies to medications?
No allergies that I know of... never had surgery before, so I don't know about anesthesia. I'm just scared about losing my finger.

Sweetheart, I want to reassure you that we're going to do everything we can to take care of your finger. The doctor will be able to tell you more about what can be done. Before I get you back to be seen, can you tell me if you're having any chest pain, trouble breathing, or feeling like your heart is racing right now?
No chest pain or trouble breathing... my heart's beating fast, but I think that's just because I'm so worried about all this.

Sweetheart, that anxiety you're feeling is completely understandable given what you've been through. I'm going to make sure you're seen by the doctor right away. Just one last thing—do you have any bleeding that's soaking through the bandage right now, or has the bleeding stopped since you wrapped it?
The bleeding stopped after I wrapped it tight... there's no fresh blood coming through now. It's just the pain and that numbness that's really getting to me.

Sweetheart, I'm going to get you to the doctor right away. You're going to be in excellent hands, and we'll do everything we can to help your finger. Let me just document everything, and we'll get you back to be seen immediately, okay?
Okay, thank you... please hurry, I really don't want to lose this finger.

Sweetheart, I want to make absolutely sure we've covered everything before I get you back. Can you tell me if you're feeling any weakness in your arm or hand, or if you're able to make a fist with your other fingers on that hand?
I can move my other fingers a little, but it hurts to try... no weakness in my arm though, just focused on that crushed finger.

Hello there! My name is James, and I'll be your triage nurse today. I'm so glad you came in to see us, because your health and well-being are our top priorities here, and we're going to take great care of you every step of the way! To get us started on the best path to getting you feeling better, could you tell me a little bit about what brought you into the emergency department today?

Um, hi James... thank you. Well, I'm mostly here because I hurt my right ankle really bad. I was just walking and, uh, I guess I tripped or twisted it, I'm not really sure exactly what happened. It just hurts so much right now, like... maybe a 7 out of 10? I'm a little anxious because it's throbbing and I can't put weight on it. Do you think I'll be able to see a doctor soon?

Oh, I am so sorry to hear about that ankle, my friend! Tripping and twisting it like that is never a fun time, and I completely understand why you're feeling a bit anxious with that throbbing 7 out of 10 pain and not being able to walk on it. Don't you worry at all, you are in the absolute best hands here! We're going to get you sorted out, get an X-ray to see exactly what's going on, and have you on the road to recovery in no time! To help me get a perfect picture of how your leg is doing, are you feeling any numbness, tingling, or coldness down in your toes on that right foot?

Um... hold on, let me try to wiggle them. No, I don't think they feel cold or, um, numb at all. They just feel like normal toes, I guess. It's really just the ankle itself that is throbbing so intensely. Wait... is it supposed to feel tingly? I'm just a little worried because it hurts so much.

No need to worry at all! It's actually a wonderful thing that your toes aren't tingly—that tells me the nerves and blood flow are doing just fine down there! Just to make absolutely sure we're getting everything taken care of today, did you happen to hit your head or hurt any other part of your body when you took that tumble?

Um... let me think for a second. No, I really don't think I hit my head or anything like that. I kind of just went down awkwardly on my leg, you know? My hands and arms feel entirely fine, so I didn't hurt them trying to catch myself either. The pain really is just all concentrated right here in my right ankle. I'm just so anxious and hoping it isn't broken or anything worse...

That is such wonderful news that you didn't hit your head or hurt anything else! It makes me so happy to hear that we can just focus all our energy on getting that ankle feeling much better. Since you're having that 7 out of 10 throbbing pain, did you happen to take any medication at home before coming in, or do you have any allergies or other medical conditions I should know about so we can get you comfortable safely?

Um... let me think. No, I didn't take any pain medicine before coming in because I wasn't sure what would be safe, and I just wanted to get here as fast as I could. Uh, as for allergies... no, I don't have any allergies to any medications that I know of. And I don't really have any medical conditions either, I'm usually pretty healthy. It's really just this ankle that is making me so upset right now. Will I be able to get something to help with the throbbing soon?

That is great to know! I promise we will get you something to help ease that throbbing pain as soon as possible. We want you feeling completely comfortable and relaxed! Just to make sure we're fully prepared, have you noticed any significant swelling, bruising, or does the ankle look deformed or bent in a weird way at all?

Um... let me look at it again. Yeah, it definitely looks pretty swollen right now, kind of puffed up like a little balloon compared to my other ankle. I think maybe it's starting to get a tiny bit purple on the outside edge, but it's a little hard for me to tell for sure. No, I don't think it looks bent in a weird way or completely out of place, thank goodness. I've just been too nervous to really touch it or move it around much because of how bad it aches.

That swelling and bruising is totally normal after taking a tumble like that, so please don't let it worry you too much! You're doing amazing, and keeping it still is exactly the right thing to do. Since we're going to get you taken care of, could you tell me if you have any scrapes or cuts on that ankle, and do you know when you had your last tetanus shot?

Um... no, I didn't see any cuts or scrapes when I looked at it, it just looks really swollen to me. The skin doesn't seem broken at all, thankfully. Uh, as for a tetanus shot... oh gosh, I really don't remember the exact last time I had one... maybe a few years ago at a checkup? I'm sorry, my memory is a little fuzzy because this throbbing pain is just distracting me so much. Would I still need a shot even if there isn't a cut?

Oh, please don't worry about the exact date of your tetanus shot right now! Since the skin isn't broken, you won't even need one today, which is one less thing to stress about! We are just going to focus on getting that X-ray done and getting some ice and pain medication on board to soothe that throbbing. Before we get you settled in, is there anybody here with you today to help you get home once we've got you all fixed up?

Um... yeah, my sister actually drove me here today. I think she's out in the waiting room right now, or... wait, maybe she is still trying to find a spot to park the car. I was just in a huge rush to get inside because of the pain, so she dropped me at the door. I was way too anxious and hurt to try driving myself, especially with it being my right foot. So, she'll definitely be here to help me get back home... I just really hope I don't end up in a cast or something.

That is wonderful that your sister is here to help you get home! We'll make sure to get her back there with you as soon as possible. While we get your room and your X-ray set up, can I get you an ice pack or a warm blanket to help keep you comfortable in the waiting area?

Um... yes, please. I think an ice pack would be really, really helpful right now. Maybe it will help calm down this swelling and, uh, the throbbing pain a little bit while I wait. A warm blanket sounds nice too, honestly, I think I'm feeling a little bit chilly from being so nervous and sitting here. I really appreciate it, James. Um... are you going to be the one taking care of me when I go back, or will it be someone else to do the X-ray?

I will absolutely get that ice pack and a nice warm blanket for you right away! To answer your question, I'll be finishing up your triage here, and then one of our fantastic emergency nurses will take over your care in the room. You'll also meet our wonderful X-ray technologist who will take those pictures of your ankle. You are going to have a whole team making sure you feel better! Just to make sure we have your complete history, do you have any past surgeries on that right leg or ankle?

Um... thank you so much, the ice pack and blanket sound really comforting right now. Uh, let me think about the surgeries... no, I am pretty sure I've never had any surgery on my right leg or my ankle before. I'm usually really careful, so this is kind of my first time taking a bad fall like this, which is probably why I'm feeling so nervous and overwhelmed. It's just throbbing so badly right now, so I'm glad to hear a whole team will be helping. Um... do you think I'll have to wait a super long time out in the waiting room before they take me back for the X-ray?

Oh, I completely understand why you're feeling a bit overwhelmed, but please know we are moving as quickly as we safely can! Wait times can fluctuate depending on who comes through our doors, but we have your ice and warm blanket coming right up to keep you comfortable while you wait. I'll get you all set up with those right now, okay?

Um... yes, please, that sounds really good. I think getting the ice right now is a great idea because it's just throbbing so much. Uh... thank you, James, for being so nice and getting those for me. I guess I'll just, um, go wait out there until my sister finishes parking and they call my name. I just really hope it goes fast and isn't broken...
I'm Nurse Patel. What brings you to the emergency department today?

Good afternoon, Nurse Patel. I've been having pain in my right leg that's been bothering me enough to come in today. It's not unbearable, but it's certainly uncomfortable and I thought it best to have it looked at properly.
Can you describe the pain? Is it sharp, dull, throbbing? And when did it start?

The pain is more of a dull, aching sort of pain, not sharp really. It started about three days ago, I believe—yes, three days. It's been fairly constant since then, though it does seem to worsen a bit when I walk.
Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth in the leg?
Yes, now that you mention it, there is some swelling around my calf area. I haven't noticed any particular redness or warmth, though. The swelling has been there since the pain started, I think.
Have you had any recent injury, surgery, or prolonged immobility? Any history of blood clots?

No recent injuries or surgeries, fortunately. I did take a rather long flight from Sydney to London about a week ago—nearly 24 hours of travel with the layover. I haven't had any history of blood clots that I'm aware of.
Have you had any shortness of breath or chest pain?
No, I haven't had any shortness of breath or chest pain, thankfully. My breathing has been perfectly normal. Is that something I should be concerned about with this leg pain?

Yes, it is a concern. The combination of leg swelling after a long flight can indicate a blood clot, which can travel to the lungs causing chest pain or shortness of breath. Are you currently taking any medications or do you have any other medical conditions?

Oh, I see—that is concerning. Yes, I take medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol; I've been on those for several years now. I also have osteoarthritis, but otherwise I'm fairly healthy for my age. Should I be worried about this being a blood clot, then?
Do you have any cancer history, recent surgery, or family history of blood clots?

No, I don't have any history of cancer and no recent surgeries as I mentioned. As for family history, I'm not entirely certain—my mother did have some issues with clotting later in life, though I don't know all the medical details. Is that relevant to what you're thinking?
How would you rate your leg pain on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain imaginable?
I'd say it's about a 5 out of 10—it's certainly uncomfortable and nagging, but I can manage it. It's not excruciating, if that's what you mean. Would you say that's moderate, then?
Have you had any fever, or do you feel warm or chilled?
No, I haven't had any fever or chills. My temperature has felt quite normal throughout this whole thing. Is fever something that typically accompanies what you're concerned about?
Are you currently able to walk, or is the pain preventing you from bearing weight on that leg?

I can still walk, yes, though it does make the pain worse when I do. I've been trying to take it easy and not walk too much, but I can bear weight on it if needed. It's more the aching that increases when I'm up and about.
Are you taking any blood thinners, or have you ever been told you have a bleeding disorder?

No, I'm not on any blood thinners—just the blood pressure and cholesterol medications I mentioned earlier. And no, I've never been told I have any bleeding disorder. Should I be on a blood thinner for this sort of thing?
Do you have any other symptoms such as unusual bleeding, new lumps, or unexplained weight loss?
No, nothing like that. I haven't had any unusual bleeding, no new lumps that I've noticed, and my weight has been quite stable. Is there something specific you're looking for with those questions?
Are you having any calf tenderness when I press here, or pain when you flex your foot upward?
Yes, it is tender when you press there—that's right where the swelling is. And yes, when I flex my foot upward like that, I do feel a pulling sort of pain in the calf. Is that significant?

Given your symptoms, travel history, and family history, I'm concerned about a possible deep vein thrombosis. You'll need imaging and lab work. I'm going to triage you now and get you registered for evaluation.

Thank you for explaining that, Nurse Patel. I must admit, hearing "deep vein thrombosis" is rather worrying. Could you please explain what exactly that imaging and lab work will involve? I'd like to understand what to expect next.
The imaging will be an ultrasound of your leg to look for clots, and blood work to check clotting factors. This is standard for suspected DVT. The team will see you shortly.
Thank you very much, Nurse Patel. That's very clear—an ultrasound and some blood work. I appreciate you taking this seriously and explaining things so thoroughly. I'll wait here then for the team.
Hello, my name is Raj, and I'm one of the triage nurses here today. I'm here to help you. Can you please tell me what brought you to the emergency department today?

Hello Raj, thank you for seeing me. I've been having thoughts about ending my life, and I knew I needed to come in and get some help. I just haven't been feeling safe at home alone with these thoughts.

I'm really glad you came in today—that took a lot of courage, and you did the right thing by seeking help. I need to ask you some important questions to make sure we keep you safe. Do you have a specific plan for how you would end your life?
Yes, I do have a plan. I've been thinking about taking all of my pills at once—I have several medications at home. That's what's been scaring me the most, that I've thought it through that much.
Thank you for being so open with me—that information is very important. I need to ask: have you taken any of those pills already today, or do you still have access to them right now?
No, I haven't taken any of them yet. They're all still at home in my medicine cabinet. I came here instead because part of me knows I don't really want to do this, and I needed someone to help me.

I appreciate your honesty and I'm so glad you reached out for help. I need to ask—have you made any suicide attempts in the past, or is this the first time you've had these kinds of thoughts with a specific plan?

This isn't the first time I've had these thoughts, but it's the first time I've had such a clear plan. Years ago, maybe ten or fifteen years back, I tried to overdose, but my husband found me and got me to the hospital in time. He passed away two years ago, and I think that's part of why this is all coming back now.

I understand this is a very difficult time for you, especially after losing your husband. You've shown a lot of strength in coming here. I need to ask—are you currently feeling like you want to act on these thoughts right now, or do you feel you can stay safe while we get you the help you need?

Right now, being here with you, I feel like I can stay safe. The urge isn't as strong as it was at home. I think just being around people and talking about it helps—I don't want to be alone with these thoughts.

I'm going to make sure we get you the immediate support you need. Before I bring in the team to help you, can you tell me if you're experiencing any physical symptoms right now—any chest pain, difficulty breathing, dizziness, or anything else that's concerning you physically?

No, I'm not having any chest pain or trouble breathing. Physically I feel okay—maybe a little tired and worn down, but nothing urgent like that. It's really just my mental state that brought me in today.

I want you to know that you're in the right place and we're going to make sure you get the care you need. Can you tell me if you've been taking any medications regularly, or if you've recently stopped or changed any medications?

Yes, I take several medications regularly. I'm on a blood pressure medication, something for my cholesterol, and an antidepressant that my doctor started me on about six months ago. I've been taking them all as prescribed—I haven't missed doses or changed anything recently.
I understand this is difficult. Can you tell me if you've used alcohol or any recreational drugs today or in the past 24 hours?
No, I haven't used any alcohol or drugs. I don't drink much—maybe a glass of wine on special occasions, but I haven't had anything in weeks. And I've never used recreational drugs.

Thank you for sharing all of that with me. You've been very helpful and brave in being so open. I'm going to make sure the mental health crisis team sees you right away. While we're getting that arranged, can you tell me—do you have any support at home, like family or friends who can be with you after you're discharged?

I have a daughter who lives about thirty minutes away—she checks in on me regularly, and I know she'd come stay with me if I asked. I also have a close friend from church who visits often. I just haven't wanted to burden them with how I've been feeling lately.

You're doing really well by being here and sharing this with me. I want to make sure we have all the information we need. Have you experienced any recent changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels that have been concerning to you?

Yes, my sleep has been terrible—I've been waking up at three or four in the morning and can't get back to sleep. My appetite is pretty much gone too; I just don't have any interest in eating. And I feel exhausted all the time, even though I'm not really doing much of anything during the day.

I'm going to make sure you're seen by our crisis team immediately. Before I do that, I just want to confirm—are you feeling any pain anywhere right now, or any physical discomfort I should know about?
No, I'm not in any physical pain right now. I'm just emotionally exhausted and drained, but there's no physical discomfort that I need to mention. Thank you for being so thorough and kind with me.

You've been incredibly brave in sharing all of this with me. I'm going to ensure the crisis team evaluates you immediately. While we arrange that, I'd like to ask—are you currently taking any other medications or supplements beyond the blood pressure, cholesterol, and antidepressant medications you mentioned?
No, those are the only medications I take regularly. I do take a daily multivitamin and calcium supplement, but that's it—nothing else beyond what I already mentioned.

I appreciate all the information you've provided. I want to make sure we have everything we need to keep you safe. Can you tell me—aside from the crisis team evaluation, are you experiencing any other medical concerns or symptoms that you feel we should address while you're here today?

No, I don't have any other medical concerns right now. My main issue is really just the suicidal thoughts and needing mental health support. Everything else physically seems to be functioning normally, so I think the crisis team is what I need most.

I understand you feel safe here with us right now. I want to make absolutely sure—if we were to discharge you today with a safety plan and follow-up, do you feel confident that you could keep yourself safe at home, or do you think you might still act on these thoughts?

I'm honestly not sure I could keep myself safe at home right now, especially at night when the thoughts get worse. I think I need more help than just a safety plan—maybe staying here for a bit where I can be monitored and get the support I need. I'm scared of what might happen if I go back home alone too soon.

I hear you, and I'm glad you're being honest about not feeling safe at home. That helps us make sure we provide the right level of care. I'm going to make sure the crisis team evaluates you immediately for possible admission. Just to help me understand your symptoms better—have you been experiencing any hallucinations or hearing voices telling you to harm yourself?

No, I haven't been hearing voices or having hallucinations. The thoughts are my own—they just feel overwhelming and constant, especially when I'm alone. It's more like a heavy darkness that won't lift rather than anything telling me what to do.
I want to make sure we have a complete picture to help you best. Can you tell me if you're currently experiencing any chest pain, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat that's concerning you?
No, I'm not having any chest pain or palpitations. My heart feels fine—it's really just my mental and emotional state that's the problem. Everything else physically seems to be okay.

Hello, my name is Mei. I'm the triage nurse here today. I know being in the emergency room can be stressful, but you are in very good hands now. Could you please tell me what brought you in to see us today?

Hello dear, thank you so much, it's so wonderful to meet you! Well, I had a little tumble at home and cut myself, but wait... what was I saying? Oh yes, I was just telling my grandson Elias about my sister in Beirut who always made the absolute best baklava with extra honey and pistachios. Anyway, I think I just tripped over the edge of the living room rug, and now I have this cut right here. It really doesn't hurt too terribly much, but my lovely daughter insisted I come see you.

Oh, sweetheart, I'm so sorry you had a fall, but I'm so glad your daughter brought you in. A cut can be quite a nuisance! Can you tell me if you hit your head when you fell, or if you take any blood-thinning medications?

Let me think... did I bump my head, dear? I don't believe so, seeing as my hair doesn't feel all messed up, thank goodness. Blood thinners, you asked? I do take a few little pills with my morning tea, but oh, you know my neighbor Mrs. Khoury takes these little pink ones and she has the most beautiful jasmine garden. The jasmine smells absolutely divine in the evenings when we sit out on the porch! I'm sorry, what were we talking about... oh yes, I take some medicine for my heart, but I simply can't recall the name right now.

Jasmine gardens are truly wonderful, sweetheart. It sounds so peaceful. Since you take heart medication, I want to be extra careful. Do you happen to have your medication bottles or a list with you? And is your lovely daughter here in the waiting room with you today? I'd love to ask her a quick question.

Oh, yes dear, my lovely Rania is right out there in the waiting area, sipping on some coffee. I didn't bring the medicine bottles myself, but I do have this deep leather handbag with me today. I bought it at a beautiful market years ago, and it holds so many things, but... oh my, what was I supposed to be looking for inside it? I am so sorry, I completely lost my train of thought just now! Rania would definitely know all the names of my heart medications, though, because she fills up my little plastic pillbox every Sunday evening while we watch our television shows.

You are doing wonderfully, sweetheart. I will ask Rania to pop back here so she can sit with you and help me with that medication list. In the meantime, could you show me exactly where you cut yourself and tell me if it is still bleeding?

Yes, dear, let me show you... it's right here on my arm. Rania wrapped this lovely little cloth around it before we left the house. Oh, looking at this cloth reminds me of the dress I wore to my cousin's wedding in Tripoli! It had the most delicate lace trim that took weeks to stitch by hand, all along the hem and the sleeves. My goodness, what was I saying? Oh, right! The cut. Let me peek under here... it looks like it's still bleeding just a little bit, but nothing to fuss over, really.

Oh, sweetheart, I am going to take a gentle look at that arm right now. Don't you worry about a thing. While we wait for your daughter to come back and help us with the medications, can you tell me if you felt dizzy right before you fell, or if you feel a little more forgetful than usual today?

Dizzy? Oh, no dear, I didn't feel dizzy at all, I just caught my heel on that pesky rug. But forgetful? Well, my goodness, I do suppose my memory has been playing a few extra tricks on me today! Just this morning I was trying to find my favorite copper pot to make some spiced lentils, and I somehow ended up in the hallway closet staring at the winter coats. My late husband bought me the most gorgeous wool coat with big wooden buttons for our anniversary... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, yes, I might be a little more scatterbrained today than usual, but you are just so sweet to take care of me!

You are doing just wonderfully, sweetheart, and it's completely okay. We'll get everything sorted out once Rania comes back. Just to be absolutely sure we're taking the best care of you, did you hurt anywhere else when you fell, like your hips, legs, or back?

Oh no, sweetheart, my hips and back feel perfectly fine, heaven forbid I break a hip! My hips have always been quite strong, you know, because I used to walk up and down the hills in our village back home every single day. The cedar trees there are just magnificent, especially when the morning dew hits the branches, and we'd gather the freshest pine nuts... oh, but wait, what was I rambling about? Oh, right, the fall—my poor little arm is really the only thing bothering me, just throbbing at perhaps a five out of ten, but I can manage. Thank you so much for taking such lovely care of an old scatterbrained lady like me!

Those cedar trees must be absolutely breathtaking to see, sweetheart. I am going to have Rania come back right now so we can get that medication list sorted out and take wonderful care of your arm. Just to be absolutely sure, besides feeling a little more scatterbrained today, have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your arms or legs, or any headache?

Weakness or numbness? Oh no dear, my arms and legs feel just fine, and my head is clear as a bell, aside from the little mix-ups today!
